newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of Dec. 16, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - Microsoft Corp's Java Software Developer's kit violates the licensing agreement it signed with Sun Microsystems Inc for the Java language, a top Sun executive told PC Week, in its December 16 issue.

Smart cards are going to become the next great frontier for lowering the cost of PC ownership while increasing security, PC Week reported December 16, and many software companies are pushing separate endeavors to promote them.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - Microsoft Corp took the covers off its transaction server software, code-named Viper, last week, but vendors, value-added resellers and analysts said the product is too immature to be effective in building enterprise applications, CRN reported December 16.
Pressure is building on Netscape Communications Corp to fully support Microsoft's Active X architecture, independent software developers and VARs told CRN.

INFOWORLD - Struggling Sybase Inc plans a revival in 1997 with the arrival of a database independent middleware strategy for corporate intranets that takes uses Java and enhanced parallel processing, Infoworld reported Dec. 16.

Apple Computer Inc will launch a Java-oriented server-centric operating system architecture at next month's Macworld Expo as part of a bid to tightly link Macintosh clients to a wide variety of servers.

INFORMATION WEEK - Intel Corp's 200 MHz Pentium Pro processor is in short supply, and "spot" prices for the chip have risen more than 50 percent in the past two months, Information Week reported in its Dec. 16 issue.
Security experts have discovered flaws in Microsoft Corp's Windows NT program that might not be repaired until version 5.0 of the operating system, Information Week reported Dec 16.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS' NEWS - At least three of the world's largest DRAM makers have been quietly working on a new high-performance synchronous DRAM (SDRAM) technology, that could block the acceptance of Rambus Inc's DRAM technology, EBN reported in its Dec. 16 issue.

The surprise departure of Gerald Rogers as chief executive of Cyrix Corp is a sign that the struggling chip maker may be in for more trouble than outsiders suspected, and it could pave the way for its demise, analysts told EBN.

ELECTRONIC ENGINEERING TIMES - The nascent U.S. smart card makers got a needed boost last week when a group of companies led by Microsoft released a proposed standard, linking smart cards and card readers to personal computers, EE Times reported December 16.

Intel confirmed last week that it is working with Rambus Inc, a private company, to develop a 1.6 gigabyte per second DRAM main memory interface for personal computers, an effort that is intended to satisfy by early 1999 what Intel said is the insatiable need for memory bandwidth.

COMPUTER RETAIL WEEK - Personal computer makers plan to hop on the Intel Corp multimedia bandwagon in a big way in January, but early 1997 systems will also include a smattering of digital cameras, low-end price points and non-Intel processors, Computer Retail Week reported Dec. 16.

Tandy Corp will redouble its in-store focus on IBM's Aptiva products in RadioShack stores next year, while retreating from the audio and video products it blames for recent comparable store sales declines, CRW reported.

MACWEEK - Apple Computer next month will take the wraps off a limited edition, high style Macintosh, code-named Spartacus, which will also carry a tony price, celebrating its founding 2 decades ago, MacWeek reported December 16.

Current estimates for the pricing are between $8,000 and $10,000 and the projected production will be 10,000 units. Spartacus will reportedly be a thin, slightly curved slab, with a 12.5 active-matrix color screen and front-mounted CD-ROM drive, in a charcoal gray unit with built-in speakers.
